hooks.text: A truck-sized space rock bounced right off Earth's atmosphere.
How did a meteoroid skip across the sky and escape?
One hundred seconds in the atmosphere before returning to space.

title: The Asteroid That Skipped Across Earth's Sky
description: Discover how a truck-sized meteoroid bounced off Earth's atmosphere in broad daylight and escaped back into space.

beats.text: A truck-sized space rock bounced right off Earth's atmosphere.
beats.visual: Artist concept of an Earth-grazing meteoroid in upper atmosphere, 1972

beats.text: On August 10, 1972, the massive object entered the upper sky over Utah in broad daylight.
beats.visual: Map of western United States and Canada showing Utah to Alberta trajectory, 1972
queries: Map of western United States and Canada

beats.text: It moved at an incredible blazing speed of about 15 kilometers per second across the western states.
beats.visual: Atmospheric entry ablation diagram of a stony meteoroid, 1972

beats.text: Cameras in Wyoming captured the glowing fireball as startled witnesses heard tremendous double sonic booms echo below.
beats.visual: Grand Teton National Park landscape view behind Jackson Lake, Wyoming, 1972

beats.text: The entire dramatic atmospheric passage lasted approximately 100 seconds from start to finish.
beats.visual: Weather satellite view of North America showing infrared sensor coverage, 1972
queries: Weather satellite view of North America

beats.text: Instead of crashing into the terrain, the heavy rock climbed right back out into space over Alberta, Canada.
beats.visual: Apollo asteroid orbit diagram showing atmospheric grazing path, 1994

beats.text: No fragments ever landed because a colossal truck-sized space rock bounced right off Earth's atmosphere.
beats.visual: Stony meteorite specimen close up studio photograph, 1994
